note:
GHOST VALUES -- example arguments, keyed by PARAMETER NAME then by TYPE. Merged into Deploy/OURONET-REGISTRY.json by REPL/tools/_registry.py; that file is generated and this one is not, so regenerating can never destroy these.

WHY BY PARAMETER AND NOT BY ENTRYPOINT. 423 entrypoints share 2,182 parameter slots but only 276 distinct names, and four names -- patron, executor, id, executee -- cover half of them. Authoring per entrypoint would mean writing the same account 416 times and getting it wrong somewhere.

THESE ARE ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT A TEST FIXTURE. Every id below was read from MAINNET so the SHAPE is real -- a consumer can see that a swpair is a four-segment pipe-joined string and an account is a glyph string, not a k: address. Do not submit them: the accounts are not yours to sign for, and an amount of 1.0 is a placeholder, not a sensible default.

chainSourced.how: DALOS.UR_OuroborosID / UR_AurynID / UR_EliteAurynID / UR_DemiurgoiID, SWP.URC_Swpairs, DPTF.UR_KEYS, DPOF.UR_KEYS, ATS.UR_KEYS. The KEYS readers return COMPOSITE `id|account` rows, so the bare id is the first pipe segment -- except DPOF's, which is `H|id|account` and needs the second.

guard.why: a guard is passed as `(read-keyset "ks")` -- this is the NAME of the transaction-data key, not the keyset. Put {"keys": [...], "pred": "keys-all"} in the transaction's `data` under that name. Inlining the keyset object is not a thing Pact accepts.

object.why: UNTYPED in the signature, so there is no schema to derive a shape from. Read the entrypoint's @doc -- an empty object here means 'the contract did not say', not 'send nothing'.

[object].why: untyped list-of-object; see the note on `object`.
